**How associating partners with Allah and obeying Satan ruins both worlds.**

(and whoever sets up partners in worship with Allah, has indeed strayed far away.) means, he will have taken other than the true path, deviated from guidance and righteousness, destroyed himself in this life and the Hereafter, and lost contentment in this life and the Hereafter. (and they invoke nothing but Shaytan, a persistent rebel!) means, Shaytan has commanded them to do this and made it seem fair and beautiful in their eyes. (And whoever takes Shaytan as a Wali (protector or helper) instead of Allah, has surely suffered a manifest loss.) means, he will have lost this life and the Hereafter. The verses that follow take up their beliefs and point out to the punishment they will face. As for the verse before us , the addressees were the pagans of Makkah who did not have the background of any Book or Prophet before that time, but the rational arguments in support of the Oneness of Allah were all too clear. Taking stones crafted with their own hands as their objects of worship was something ineffectual, false and erroneous even in the sight of someone with ordinary common-sense. The Holy Qur'an has reported the words of the disbelievers they shall utter on arrival into the Jahannam: By Allah, we were in obvious error when we had equated you with Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.

**The emptiness of satanic promises and superstition when facing divine judgment.**

Man’s real challenge in this world is from Satan. Though Satan has no real power, he can lure human beings with fanciful promises to fulfil wishful, imaginary desires and thus manage to make them deviate from the straight path of truth. Satan’s way of misguiding is of two main types: one is superstition and the other is interference in God’s creation. Faith in superstition means expectation of such results from something as have no relation with that thing. (and Shaytan's promises are nothing but deceptions.) Allah states that on the Day of Return,. (And Shaytan will say when the matter has been decided: "Verily, Allah promised you a promise of truth. And I too promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you)[14:22], until,.

122.text:
In direct contrast to the hundred and twenty-first verse's decree of inescapable Hell for the followers of Satan's delusions, the hundred and twenty-second verse proclaims the unfailing promise of Allah to His faithful and obedient servants. "And those who believe and do good, We will soon admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow" pairs genuine inward faith in Allah, His Messenger, and the Qur'an with outward acts of obedience that draw a servant close to his Lord, promising that Allah will bring them into the palaces and orchards of Paradise beneath which rivers of water, milk, wine, and honey flow wherever they wish. "to stay there for ever and ever. Allah’s promise is ˹always˺ true" contrasts the fleeting, deceptive promises of Satan in verse 120 with the absolute certainty of Allah's word: the believers will abide in Paradise eternally, never dying and never being removed from its bliss, because Allah Himself has guaranteed it in truth. "And whose word is more truthful than Allah’s" seals the comparison with a rhetorical question that admits only one answer—none is truer in statement, news, or promise than Allah, as the Prophet regularly proclaimed in his sermons—before the hundred and twenty-third verse warns that divine grace is earned by faith and deeds rather than communal boasting or wishful thinking.

**Eternal Gardens beneath which rivers flow for those who combine faith with righteous deeds.**

But those who believe and perform righteous deeds We shall admit them to Gardens underneath which rivers flow abiding therein for ever; God’s promise in truth that is God promised them this and fulfilled it in truth; and who that is and none is truer in utterance that is in statement than God? (But as for those who believe) in Muhammad and the Qur'an (and do good works) i.e. acts of obedience, in relation to that which binds them to their Lord (We shall bring them into Gardens underneath which) beneath its rooms and habitations (rivers) of wine, water, milk and honey (flow, wherein they will abide) they will abide in Paradise, never to die or be removed (for ever. It is a promise from Allah) regarding Paradise and hell (in truth) which shall truly happen; (and who can be more truthful than Allah in utterance) in promise? I will enter those who have faith in Me and do good actions that bring them close to Me into gardens with palaces overlooking flowing streams, where they will live eternally. Allah then mentions the condition of the content righteous believers and the perfect honor they will earn in the end. (And those who believe and do righteous good deeds,) meaning, their hearts were truthful and their limbs obedient with the righteous acts they were commanded, all the while abandoning the evil they were prohibited from doing. (We shall admit them to Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise) meaning, they will think of where they want these rivers to flow and they will flow there,. (to dwell therein forever), without end or being removed from it. But those who believe and perform righteous deeds We shall admit them to gardens underneath which rivers flow abiding therein for ever; God's promise in truth; and who is truer in utterance than Godḍ Those whom We have made fortunate by [Our] decree and speech asʿadnāhum ḥukman wa-qawlan were helped at the time We brought them into existence by [Our] generosity and power awjadnāhum kara man wa-Ṭawlan.

**Why Allah's promise is the absolute truth and no speech is truer than His word.**

No one is more true then Him in His statements and promises. (And Shaytan will say when the matter has been decided: "Verily, Allah promised you a promise of truth. And I too promised you, but I betrayed you. I had no authority over you)[14:22], until,. (Allah's promise is the truth), meaning, this is a true promise from Allah, and verily, Allah's promise shall come to pass. (and whose words can be truer than those of Allah) meaning, none is more truthful in statement and narration than Allah. There is no deity worthy of worship, or Lord except Him. The Messenger of Allah used to proclaim in his speech,. (The most truthful speech is Allah's Speech, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The worst matters are the newly invented (in religion), every newly invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is a heresy, and every heresy is in the Fire.)

**Directing devotion exclusively to Allah and rejecting polytheism and satanic interference.**

As for the verse before us , the addressees were the pagans of Makkah who did not have the background of any Book or Prophet before that time, but the rational arguments in support of the Oneness of Allah were all too clear. The first kind of injustice is Shirk, the ascribing of a partner to Allah; the second kind of injustice is falling short in fulfilling the rights of Allah, known as Huququllah; and the third kind of injustice is the contravention of the rights of Allah's created beings against each other, known as Huququl-‘Ibad. To consider any created being other than Allah equal to Allah in worship, or in love and reverence, is what Shirk really is. Another way of Satan’s misleading man is by interfering in the divine scheme of things. God has created man with the innate desire to direct all his attention to God. Interfering with this involves diverting man’s attention towards things other than God or else encouraging him to acquire things by other self-devised ways and not through the natural course set by God (for instance, homosexuality). In this manner Satan interferes with man’s observance of God’s divine plan for the entire universe.

123.text:
Following the hundred and twenty-second verse's declaration that Allah's promise of Paradise is absolute truth, the hundred and twenty-third verse was revealed when Muslims and the People of the Book sat together boasting of their communal labels—the Jews and Christians claiming superiority because their prophets and scriptures came earlier, and some Muslims replying that their Prophet and Book came last—and it establishes that salvation rests on sincere faith and action rather than group pride. "˹Divine grace is˺ neither by your wishes nor those of the People of the Book!" sweeps aside every form of religious complacency and wishful thinking, whether the fancies of the People of the Book that their sins of the day are automatically forgiven at night, or the assumption of any believer that mere formal affiliation with a prophet or community guarantees safety without obedience. "Whoever commits evil will be rewarded accordingly" lays down the impartial law of accountability that initially made the closest companions of the Prophet tremble until the Prophet comforted them: while the unrepentant disbeliever faces his full requital in the Hereafter, the believing servant who slips into fault is purified and requited even through the worries, illnesses, and thorns that prick his foot in this world. "and they will find no protector or helper besides Allah" warns that no lineage, saint, or partisan group can shield an unrepentant wrongdoer from Allah's decree unless he turns back to Allah in repentance, proving that in the court of the All-Just Judge every soul stands accountable for what resides in its heart and what its hands have earned rather than the slogans of its group, just as the planter of bitter colocynth never harvests roses and the drinker of poison never tastes honey, so too no community can harvest divine nearness while squandering the duty of obedience, before the hundred and twenty-fourth verse pairs this warning with the glad tidings for every believing man and woman who does good.

**The dispute of communal boasting between Muslims and the People of the Book.**

When the Muslims and the People of the Scripture began to pride themselves upon God’s promise the following was revealed It this matter is not dependent upon your desires nor the desires of the People of the Scripture but upon righteous deeds. (It will not be in accordance with your desires) it is not as you desire, O believers, that no harm shall come to you after you have accepted the faith, (nor the desires of the People of the Scripture) nor is it as the people of the Book desire when they say: �whatever sins we commit during the day will be forgiven at night, and whatever sins we commit during the night will be forgiven in the day�. The issue of salvation and success O Muslims is not dependent on mere hopes and desires, nor in what the People of the Scripture hope and wish for; rather, it is based on action. The people of the Book, the adherents of the Torah and the adherents of the Gospel, as well as the adherents of other religions sat together one day and each claimed that they were better than the others. One day, the Muslims and the people of the Book argued with each other. We are more guided than you and have a better right to Allah than you. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. Allah, exalted is He, later backed the argument of the Muslims against their opponents from amongst the adherents of other religions with His words (And whoso doeth good works, whether of male or female) [4:124] and His words (Who is better in religion than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah) [4:125] . People of the Scriptures said, 'Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book before your Book. Verse 123 which begins with the words: 'This is not (a matter of) your fancies or the fancies of the People of the Book...', is about a cross talk between Muslims and the People of the Book. According to Sayyidna Qatadah once it so happened that some Muslims and the People of the Book started talking to each other in a vainglorious strain. The People of the Book said that they were superior to Muslims because their Prophet came before the Prophet of Islam and that their Book appeared before the Qur'an of Muslims did.

**Why salvation depends on truth in the heart and righteous deeds rather than wishful thinking.**

This Ayah indicates that the religion is not accepted on account of wishful thinking or mere hopes. Rather, the accepted religion relies on what resides in the heart and which is made truthful through actions. It is not true that when one utters a claim to something, he attains it merely on account of his claim. It is not true that every person who claims to be on the truth is considered as such, merely on account of his words, until his claim gains merit with proof from Allah. (It will not be in accordance with your desires, nor those of the People of the Scripture, whosoever works evil, will have the recompense thereof)[4:123], meaning safety will not be acquired by you or them just by wishful thinking. Rather, the key is in obeying Allah and following what He has legislated through the words of His honorable Messengers. On the contrary, they should be concerned with what they actually do, for their success will not come solely on the basis of their formal adherence to a given Prophet and a Book. When the People of the Book, that is, believers in God and the Hereafter, become engrossed in the world, they do not do so by refusing to believe in God and the existence of the Hereafter. What they do is believe in these realities in the formal sense while, in practice, devoting all their efforts to worldly acquisition. But for the attainment of Paradise, wishful thinking alone is believed to suffice. For instance, through the blessing of some saint, association with a certain group, recitation of some words and phrases, in short, by such cheap formulae or superficial actions, it is hoped that they will be saved from the raging fire of Hell and be ushered into Heaven. God’s system is established on such firm grounds that all divine verdicts are based on realities and not on wishful thinking.

**How every evil deed is requited and how worldly trials expiate the believer's sins.**

Whoever does evil shall be requited for it either in the Hereafter or in this life through trials and tribulations as is stated in hadīth; and he will not find besides God that is other than Him any friend to protect him or helper to defend him against Him. (He who doeth wrong) evil (will have the recompense thereof) the believers will be recompensed in this world or after death before entering Paradise, and the unbelievers in the Hereafter before entering hell, (and will not find against Allah) against the torment of Allah (any protecting friend) any relative to benefit him (or helper) to save him from the torment. Whoever, from amongst you, does an evil action will be rewarded for it on the Day of Judgement. They will not find any friend to bring any benefit to them nor any helper to protect them from harm. (So whosoever does good equal to the weight of an atom, shall see it. And whosoever does evil equal to the weight of an atom, shall see it.)[99:7-8] and it was reported that when these Ayat were revealed, they became hard on many Companions. I know the hardest Ayah in the Qur'an.' He said, 'What is it, O 'A'ishah!' I said,. (That is what strikes the believing servant, even the problems that bother him.)" Ibn Jarir and Abu Dawud also recorded this Hadith. (whosoever works evil, will have the recompense thereof,) was revealed, it was hard on Muslims. (Be steadfast and seek closeness. Everything that afflicts the Muslim, even the thorn that pierces his skin and the hardship he suffers, will be an expiation for him.)" 'Ali bin Abi Talhah reported that Ibn 'Abbas said; "Unless he repents and Allah forgives him. When this verse was revealed "And whoever does evil shall be requited for it", we were deeply grieved and concerned. Keep doing what you can to the best of your ability for (the punishment mentioned here does not necessarily have to be that of Hell, instead) whatever hardship or pain which afflicts you makes amends for your sins and requites your evil deeds, to the limit that even a thorn which pinches someone's foot becomes an expiation of some sin.'. Now, if every evil deed has to be requited, who can hope to go unscathed from among us?' He said: '0 Abu Bakr, you and your believing brothers need not worry about it because worldly hardships that you face shall make amends for your sins.'. It is not your desires nor the desires of the people of the scripture. Whoever plants colocynth will not harvest roses and jasmine. Whoever drinks deadly poison will not find the taste of honey. Likewise whoever squanders the duty of service will not become firmly established on the carpet of nearness. Whomever the divine decree rejects wa-man nafathu al-qaḌiyyati there is no helper for him in creation fa-lā nāṣira lahu min al-bariyyati.

124.text:
Balancing the hundred and twenty-third verse's warning that whoever commits evil will be requited for it and that wishful thinking saves no one, the hundred and twenty-fourth verse sets forth the positive half of divine justice by guaranteeing full reward to every person who combines sound faith with righteous action. "But those who do good—whether male or female—" affirms that in Allah's court men and women stand on equal footing in earning eternal felicity through acts of obedience, charity, and service to God. "and have faith will enter Paradise and will never be wronged ˹even as much as˺ the speck on a date stone" stipulates the essential condition that makes good works acceptable—genuine faith in Allah and His Messenger—and promises that those who unite faith with practice will be admitted into Paradise without having their reward diminished by even the tiniest dint or pit on the back of a date-stone, demonstrating that whereas good works lacking sound faith have no weight in the Hereafter and formal faith without righteous deeds is empty wishful thinking, the union of true belief and obedient action secures Allah's generous and unfailing reward for every man and woman alike, without the slightest favouritism or diminution of what they laboured to earn in Allah's service, before the hundred and twenty-fifth verse defines the highest rank of religion through the sincere submission of Abraham.

**Combining genuine faith with righteous deeds for both men and women to enter Paradise.**

And whoever does any righteous deeds whether male or female and is a believer — such shall be admitted into read passive yudkhalūna or active yadkhulūna ‘they shall enter’ Paradise and not be wronged by as much as the dint in a date-stone. (And whoso doeth good works) acts of obedience, relating to that which is between him and his Lord, (whether of male or female, and he (or she) is a believer) while being a believer who is genuine in his or her faith, (such will enter Paradise and they will not be wronged the dint in a date stone) their rewards will not be diminished even if it be by the size of the dint in a date stone. Any person, whether male or female, who does good actions and has true faith in Allah will enter Paradise, because they combined faith with practice. The reward of their actions will not be reduced in the least, not even to the extent of a speck on a date stone. (And whoever does righteous good deeds, male or female, and is a believer). Allah then mentions His kindness, generosity and mercy in accepting the good deeds from His servants, whether male or female, with the condition that they embrace the faith. He also stated that He will admit the believers into Paradise and will not withhold any of their righteous deeds, even the weight of a Naqir - speck on the back of a date-stone. Earlier, we discussed the 'Fatīl' - the scalish thread in the long slit of a date-stone, and both of these, along with the 'Qiṭmīr' – the thin membrane over the date-stone were mentioned in the Qur'an. It means a man or woman who does good deeds, subject to the condition that such deeds issue forth from true faith, shall certainly go to Paradise fully rewarded for all his or her deeds without being wronged in the least. The hint given here is that the People of the Book or other non-Muslims may also have some good deeds of their own, but, since their faith is not sound, therefore, those deeds of theirs are not acceptable. As for Muslims, since their faith is sound and their deeds too are good, therefore, they are the successful ones, and superior to others. Allah, exalted is He, later backed the argument of the Muslims against their opponents from amongst the adherents of other religions with His words (And whoso doeth good works, whether of male or female) [4:124] and His words (Who is better in religion than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah) [4:125] .

**Why divine justice rewards service in full and rejects empty wishful thinking.**

Whoever does evil shall be requited for it; and he will not find besides God any friend or helper. And whoever does righteous deeds whether male or female and is a believer-such shall be admitted into paradise and not be wronged the dint in a date-stone. Whoever plants colocynth will not harvest roses and jasmine. Whoever drinks deadly poison will not find the taste of honey. Likewise whoever squanders the duty of service will not become firmly established on the carpet of nearness. Whoever labors in Our service khidma will not be kept from attaining Our blessing niʿma. But for the attainment of Paradise, wishful thinking alone is believed to suffice. For instance, through the blessing of some saint, association with a certain group, recitation of some words and phrases, in short, by such cheap formulae or superficial actions, it is hoped that they will be saved from the raging fire of Hell and be ushered into Heaven. Such wishful thinking, in whatever beautiful words it may have been couched, is not going to come to their rescue. In God’s court everyone will be judged exactly in accordance with his actions. There will be nothing other than the law of justice promulgated by God Himself to influence His decisions.

**How the two components of sound faith and following what Allah legislated prevent error and wishful thinking.**

The fourth verse lays down a criterion to help determine correctly as to who is acceptable in the sight of Allah, and who is not. Any shortfall in either of the two components makes all efforts go waste. A careful look will reveal that all strayings into error and evil, wherever they may be in this wide world, are triggered because of a shortfall in one of these two components. You will come across the same two points of reference - any deviation from either is bound to land one in disgrace. Rather, the accepted religion relies on what resides in the heart and which is made truthful through actions. (It will not be in accordance with your desires, nor those of the People of the Scripture, whosoever works evil, will have the recompense thereof)[4:123], meaning safety will not be acquired by you or them just by wishful thinking. Rather, the key is in obeying Allah and following what He has legislated through the words of His honorable Messengers.

125.text:
Completing the answer to the competing boasts of religious communities in verses 123 and 124, the hundred and twenty-fifth verse sets forth the universal criterion of the best religion in the sight of Allah and anchors it in the example of Abraham, whom every scripture-bearing community revered. "And who is better in faith than those who ˹fully˺ submit themselves to Allah, do good, and follow the Way of Abraham, the upright?" establishes that no human being has a fairer or firmer religion than one who unites the two pillars of accepted worship: first, surrendering his face, heart, and purpose exclusively to Allah in pure sincerity uncontaminated by hypocrisy or worldly show; and second, doing good by following the prophetic guidance and sacred law revealed by Allah rather than self-invented customs, walking upon the upright monotheistic creed of Abraham that turns away from every false deity toward the One Creator. "Allah chose Abraham as a close friend" honors Abraham with the title of Khalil—the intimate friend whose heart was filled with pure love and total obedience when tested by his Lord—and reminds the world that Muhammad, whom Allah likewise chose as His Khalil, is the truest heir of Abraham's way, showing that just as a jewel has no worth without its lustre, outward deeds have no life without inward purification of intention for Allah alone and strict adherence to the example of His Messenger, and proving against every sectarian claim of the Jews, the Christians, and the Arab idolaters that the true followers of Abraham are those who turn their whole existence to God in humility, justice, and unswerving monotheism rather than those who merely claim his name while abandoning his creed and the final Messenger who renewed it, before the hundred and twenty-sixth verse proclaims Allah's absolute ownership and knowledge of all things in the heavens and the earth.

**The two pillars of accepted religion: sincere submission to Allah and following prophetic guidance.**

And who that is and none is fairer in religion than he who submits his purpose that is than he who is compliant and offers his deeds sincerely to God and is virtuous and declares God’s Oneness and who follows the creed of Abraham the one that is in accordance with the creed of Islam as a hanīf? hanīfan is a circumstantial qualifier that is to say one inclining away from all religions to the upright religion. (Who is better in religion) who is firmer in religion and better in speech (than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah) than him whose Religion and works are sincerely devoted to Allah (while doing good (to men) good in deed and speech (and follows the tradition of Abraham, the upright) who surrendered completely to Allah? No one is better in religion than the one who surrenders to Allah outwardly and inwardly, does good actions and follows the religion of Abraham, which forms the basis of the religion of Muhammad ﷺ: inclining away from idolatry and disbelief to monotheism and faith. (And who can be better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah.) meaning, performs the good actions in sincerity for his Lord with faith and awaiting the reward with Allah,. (and he is a Muhsin) following the correct guidance that Allah legislated in the religion of truth which He sent His Messenger with. These are the two conditions, in the absence of which no deed will be accepted from anyone; sincerity and correctness. The work is sincere when it is performed for Allah alone and it becomes correct when it conforms to the Shari'ah. So, the deed becomes outwardly correct with following the Sunnah and inwardly correct with sincerity. When any deed lacks either of these two conditions, the deed becomes null and void. For instance, when one lacks the pillar of sincerity in his work, he becomes a hypocrite who shows off for people. Whoever does not follow the Shari'ah, he becomes an ignorant, wicked person. When one combines both pillars, his actions will be the deeds of the faithful believers whose best deeds are accepted from them and their errors erased. And who is better in Faith than one who has surrendered his self to Allah and is good in deeds, and has followed the creed of Ibrahim, the upright... It means that there can be no way better than the way of the person who is an embodiment of two virtues: Firstly, 'surrenders his or her self to Allah.' In other words, acts for the good pleasure of Allah with all sincerity at one's command without ever contaminating one's deeds with hypocritical or materialistic motives. Those referred to as (who incurred { Your) wrath) are people who lack sincerity, and those called (who have gone astray) are those who have not acted right. They think a good deed is a good deed and could be done at one's choice although the Holy Qur'an and the Sunnah have made it perfectly clear that good conduct depends exclusively on the teachings of the Holy Prophet and on following the Sunnah, the example set by him. It is, rather, pointing out to the doing of good deeds - and a good deed is nothing but what is done in accordance with the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet .

**Following the upright monotheism of Abraham whom Allah chose as an intimate friend.**

And God took Abraham for a close friend as His elect one whose love for Him is pure. The people of the Book, the adherents of the Torah and the adherents of the Gospel, as well as the adherents of other religions sat together one day and each claimed that they were better than the others. Allah, exalted is He, later backed the argument of the Muslims against their opponents from amongst the adherents of other religions with His words (And whoso doeth good works, whether of male or female) [4:124] and His words (Who is better in religion than he who surrendereth his purpose to Allah) [4:125] . (And follows the religion of Ibrahim the Hanif (Monotheist).) referring to Muhammad and his following, until the Day of Resurrection. (Verily, among mankind who have the best claim to Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet), [3:68] and,. (Then, We have sent the Revelation to you (saying): "Follow the religion of Ibrahim the Hanif (Monotheist) and he was not of the Mushrikin). [16:123]. The Hanif, intentionally and with knowledge, avoids Shirk, he goes attentively to the truth, allowing no one to hinder him or stop him from it. (And Allah did take Ibrahim as a Khalil (an intimate friend)!) encourages following Ibrahim Al-Khalil, because he was and still is an Imam whose conduct is followed and imitated. Indeed, Ibrahim reached the ultimate closeness to Allah that the servants seek, for he attained the grade of Khalil, which is the highest grade of love. He acquired all this due to his obedience to His Lord, just as Allah has described him,. (And (remember) when the Lord of Ibrahim tried him with (certain) commands, which he fulfilled)[2:124], and,. (Verily, Ibrahim was an Ummah, obedient to Allah, a Hanif, and he was not one of the Mushrikin). [16:120]. Ibrahim was called Allah's Khalil due to his Lord's great love towards him, on account of the acts of obedience he performed that Allah loves and prefers. (Allah has chosen me as His Khalil, just as He has chosen Ibrahim as His Khalil.) Allah's statement,.

**Purifying the heart's intention and turning one's whole existence toward God.**

Who is more beautiful in religion than he who submits his face to God while he is a beautiful-doer and follows the creed of Abraham, an unswerving man? In this verse the Lord of the Worlds, the God of the world's folk, the Enactor who knows the hid den, praises the self-purifiers and shows that He is pleased with self-purification in deeds. The first person to dress the Kaabah of deeds in the cloak of self-purification was MuṣṬafā, who said, "Deeds are only through intentions. " Self-purification in deeds does the work of color in jewels. Just as a jewel without the cape of color is a worthless stone, so also deeds without self-purification is to knock oneself out without hitting the mark. The work is done by self-purification, salvation lies in self-purification, and endless felicity lies in self-purification, but self-purification itself is exalted and does not come down just any where, nor does it show its face to just anyone. The Exalted Lord said, "It is one of My secrets that I deposit in the hearts of those whom I love among My servants. Who is that servant of God upon whom God will shower His blessings? It is believers like Abraham who submit themselves fully to their Lord; who reserve their loyalties exclusively for God; who carry out their affairs in the world with justice and modesty, scrupulously avoiding injustice and arrogance. Turning one’s face towards God means turning towards Him with one’s whole existence. If one were to realize that human beings are utterly powerless, one would experience the same state of utter helplessness as one will undergo on the Day of Judgement, when all the realities are laid bare before one.

126.text:
Sealing the passage on true religion and the friendship of Abraham (`4:123–125`), the hundred and twenty-sixth verse answers any lingering wonder as to how a mortal servant can attain nearness to the Creator while reminding humanity of Allah's absolute sovereignty and all-encompassing knowledge. "To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth" proclaims that every angel, prophet, human being, and marvel in the upper and lower worlds is Allah's possession, creation, and servant under His sole authority, so that He has no need of anyone's obedience, none can question His decree when He chooses an upright servant like Abraham or Muhammad for His friendship, and every creature owes Him complete submission. "And Allah is Fully Aware of everything" affirms that Allah's knowledge and power surround all things in the heavens and the earth—not even the weight of an atom or a secret intention in a worshipper's heart escapes His observation—before the hundred and twenty-seventh verse returns to the practical social legislation of the surah to protect orphan women and helpless children.

**Allah's sole ownership of the heavens and the earth and His all-encompassing knowledge.**

To God belongs all that is in the heavens and in the earth as possessions creatures and servants; and God is ever the Encompasser of all things in knowledge and power that is He is ever possessed of such attributes. (Unto Allah belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth) of created beings and marvels: they are all his bondsmen and bondswomen. (Allah ever surroundeth) has the knowledge of (all things) in relation to the dwellers of the heavens and the earth. Allah, with His knowledge, power and planning, surrounds everything in His creation. (And to Allah belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth.) means, everything and everyone are His property, servants and creation, and He has full authority over all of this. There is no one who can avert Allah's decision or question His judgment. He is never asked about what He does due to His might, ability, fairness, wisdom, compassion and mercy. (And Allah is Ever Encompassing all things.) means, His knowledge encompasses everything and nothing concerning His servants is ever hidden from Him. Nothing, even the weight of an atom, ever escapes His observation in the heavens and earth, nor anything smaller or bigger than that.

**How Allah's sovereignty admonishes servants to fulfill His rights with sincerity and prophetic practice.**

In these verses, He says three times "To God belongs everything in the heavens and everything in the earth. The first is an admonishment for the common Muslims, the second an admonishment for the wor shipful servants and godwary, and the third an admonishment for the sincerely truthful and elect. First He says for the common Muslims, "Everything in heaven and earth is My possession and kingdom. My knowledge reaches all and I am aware of all. I have made certain rightful dues incumbent among you and set apart obligatory acts for you. Does He who created not know, while He is the Gentle, the Aware? [67:14]. Firstly, 'surrenders his or her self to Allah.' In other words, acts for the good pleasure of Allah with all sincerity at one's command without ever contaminating one's deeds with hypocritical or materialistic motives. According to the great commentator, Ibn Kathir., the way in which one acts, the correct way, means that it will not be some self-invented way. Ignorant people do this with 'sincerity' as an act of worship worthy of the reward and pleasure of Allah, but the deed of such a person goes waste or becomes even sinful in the light of the Shari'ah bequeathed by the noble Prophet . There-fore, in all our deeds relating to Salah, Sawm, Hajj, Zakah, Sadaqat, Khayrat, Dhikr of Allah, Salah (durud) and Salam, it is necessary to keep in mind the way these were done by the Messenger of Allah and how he told us to do them. By saying: ‌ (And Allah has made Ibrahim a friend), it has been hinted that this high station bestowed on Sayyidna Ibrahim has good reason behind it for he was absolutely and superbly sincere and his deed too was sound and correct with intimation from Allah.

**Submitting to the unseen Lord like Abraham and realizing human powerlessness before the Day of Judgment.**

Who is that servant of God upon whom God will shower His blessings? It is believers like Abraham who submit themselves fully to their Lord; who reserve their loyalties exclusively for God; who carry out their affairs in the world with justice and modesty, scrupulously avoiding injustice and arrogance. Turning one’s face towards God means turning towards Him with one’s whole existence. However, He has chosen to remain invisible in this world. Man commits all kinds of evil deeds, because he does not see God. He assumes that he is free to do as he pleases. If one were to realize that human beings are utterly powerless, one would experience the same state of utter helplessness as one will undergo on the Day of Judgement, when all the realities are laid bare before one.

127.text:
Returning to the core theme that opened Surah An-Nisāʾ—protecting the rights of women, orphan girls, and helpless children—the hundred and twenty-seventh verse was revealed when people came to the Prophet asking for legal pronouncements regarding women and their inheritance after the earlier verses had outlawed the pre-Islamic abuses of guardians. "They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding women. Say, “It is Allah Who instructs you regarding them" announces that the Lord of the worlds Himself issues the binding legal decree concerning women's rights and duties, leaving no room for pre-Islamic custom or greedy evasion. "Instruction has ˹already˺ been revealed in the Book concerning the orphan women you deprive of their due rights but still wish to marry" points directly back to the opening verses of this surah (`4:2–3` and `4:11`) and exposes the two-faced injustice of guardians in the age of ignorance: if an orphan girl under a guardian's care was wealthy and beautiful, he desired to marry her himself without paying her a fair dowry or giving her the inheritance Allah ordained for her; and if she was unattractive, he refused to marry her yet prevented her from marrying anyone else so that her estate would never leave his hands. "also helpless children, as well as standing up for orphans’ rights" reiterates the command to give young, defenseless boys and girls their full share of inheritance—whereas pre-Islamic Arabs gave inheritance only to men who fought with the sword—and to deal with all orphans in complete equity regarding both their property and their marriage. "And whatever good you do is certainly well known to Allah.”" closes by encouraging guardians and believers to fulfill every duty of kindness and justice toward the vulnerable, assuring them that Allah knows every upright deed and intention and will reward it in full, teaching the believers that social laws bear their true fruit only when guardians and judges enforce them out of reverence for God, dread of accountability in the Hereafter, and genuine compassion for orphan girls and defenseless children whose rights were trampled in the age of ignorance, so that no guardian ever again uses marriage as a pretext to devour an orphan girl's wealth or uses her lack of beauty as an excuse to lock her away from marriage until she dies, before the hundred and twenty-eighth verse addresses how a married couple resolves estrangement within marriage.

**Allah's legal pronouncement linking back to the opening verses of the surah on orphan girls.**

They will ask you for a pronouncement concerning the matter of women and their inheritance. Say to them ‘God pronounces to you concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book the Qur’ān in the ‘inheritance’ verse Q. 411 and He also pronounces to you concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed what is obligatory for them of inheritance for you O guardians who desire not to marry them because of their ugliness and you prevent them from marrying others coveting their inheritance in other words God pronounces to you not to do this; and concerning the oppressed young children that you give them what is their due and He also commands you that you deal justly equitably with orphans with respect to inheritance and dowry. (They consult thee concerning women) they ask you about the inheritance of women; the one who asked him was 'Uyaynah. (Say: Allah giveth to you decree) expounds to you the legal ruling (concerning them) concerning their inheritance, (and the Scripture) at the beginning of this surah (which hath been recited unto you (giveth decree), concerning female orphans) the daughters of Umm Kuhhah (unto whom ye give not that which is ordained for them) that which is prescribed for them of inheritance; Allah has already explained this at the beginning of the surah (though you desire to marry them) you refrain from marrying them because they are not attractive, so now give them their wealth so that you may desire to marry them for that which they have, (and (concerning) the weak among children) and He expounds to you the inheritance of children, (and that ye should deal justly with orphans) He explains to you that you should protect justly and fairly the wealth of orphans. They ask you, O Messenger, about the rights and duties of women. Allah will clarify for you what you have asked and what is recited in the Qur’ān with respect to orphan girls in your care, to whom you do not give the dowry and the inheritance that Allah has ordained for them; and whom you do not wish to marry, yet you prevent them from getting married because of your greed for their wealth. That which has been recited unto him in the Scripture refers to the first verse in which He says (And if ye fear that ye will not deal fairly by the orphans) [4:3]. And Allah, exalted is He, says in the other verse (though ye desire to marry them), i.e. one of you desires to marry the orphan under his care when she is not of great beauty or possesses a lot of wealth. Thus, men were warned against marrying the orphaned because of their beauty or out of desire for their wealth, unless one was prepared to deal with them fairly, for the trend was that men shunned those orphans who had no wealth or were not beautiful. What is meant by Allah's saying, 'And about what is recited unto you in the Book' is the former verse which said,. (If you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry (other) women of your choice.)[4:3]" 'A'ishah said, "Allah's statement,. The guardians were forbidden to marry their orphan girls possessing property and beauty without being just to them, as they generally refrain from marrying them (when they are neither beautiful nor wealthy).

**Outlawing the two-faced abuse of orphan women and giving helpless children their inheritance.**

He also explains to you that your duty with respect to minor children who are helpless is to give them their due right of inheritance and not to wrong them by seizing their wealth. He explains to you the duty of being fair to orphans and looking after their best interests in this world and the Afterlife. Consequently, when a man is the caretaker of a female orphan, he might like to marry her himself. In this case, Allah commands him to give her a suitable dowry that other women of her status get. If he does not want to do that, then let him marry other women, for Allah has made this matter easy for Muslims. Sometimes, the caretaker does not desire to marry the orphan under his care, because she is not attractive to his eye. In this case, Allah forbids the caretaker from preventing the female orphan from marrying another man for fear that her husband would share in the money that is mutually shared between the caretaker and the girl. 'Ali bin Abi Talhah said that Ibn 'Abbas said, "During the time of Jahiliyyah, the caretaker of a female orphan would cover her with his rope, and when he did that, no man would marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired to marry her, he married her and took control of her wealth. If she was not beautiful, he did not allow her to marry until she died, and when she died he inherited her money. (and the children who are weak and oppressed,) that during the time of Jahiliyyah, they used to deny young children and females a share of inheritance. (you give not what they deserve) thus prohibiting this practice and designating a fixed share for each,. (To the male, a portion equal to that of two females..)[4:11] whether they were young or old, as Sa'id bin Jubayr and others stated. "Just as when she is beautiful and wealthy you would want to marry her and have her for yourself, so when she is not wealthy or beautiful, marry her and have her for yourself. First, and tend to marry them," which refers to the people who, attracted to the beauty of the orphan girls, used to marry them without giving them the due rights- of a wife. It refers to the people who did not marry the orphan girls because of their unattractive features, but at the same time did not let them marry others, because they wanted that their wealth should remain in their hands. At the beginning of this Surah, particular injunctions relating to orphans and women were mentioned. Also stressed there was the mandatory nature of the need to fulfill their rights. The reason was that, during the days of Jahiliyyah, some people would simply refuse to give any part of the inheritance to them, others would unlawfully eat up what they got in inheritance or through any other alternate source, still others would marry them but avoided paying full dower they were entitled to; these were practices prohibited as stated earlier. But, when there was no abrogation, they decided among themselves that they should go directly to the Holy Prophet and ask him. According to Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, this very question was the reason behind the revelation of this verse and the verses which followed carried additional rulings relating to women (Bayan al-Qur'an).

**Standing firm for orphans' rights and doing good under the watchful gaze of Allah.**

Whatever good you do God is ever Knower of it’ and He will requite you for it. (Whatever good ye do) by being kind to them, (lo! Allah is ever Aware of it) as well as of your intentions. Allah knows of any good you do towards orphans and others, and will reward you for it. (and that you stand firm for justice to orphans.) (And whatever good you do, Allah is Ever All-Aware of it.) encourages performing the good deeds and fulfilling the commandments, and states that Allah is knowledgeable of all of this and He will reward for it in the best and most perfect manner. God pronounces to you concerning them and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them for you desire to marry them and the oppressed children and that you deal justly with orphans. Whatever good you do God is ever Knower of it. He prohibited [men] from coveting that which would lead them to do harm or wrong to oppressed women and orphans. When people asked the Prophet about the injunctions of the shariah on various social matters, he was instructed by God that great emphasis must be laid on goodness, justice, fraternity and piety. This is because any law serves its purpose only when the person who has to enforce it is God-fearing and truly desirous of justice. Moreover, social reform can take place only when the evil-doer realizes that he is ultimately accountable to God and that, even if he manages to fool the people and save himself from the consequences of his crime in this world, he cannot escape from God’s grip. As for the doer of good works, he should carry on his efforts irrespective of whether or not he is appreciated by the people, in the belief that God is certainly watching him and will definitely reward him for his endeavours.

128.text:
Moving from the rights of orphan women in the hundred and twenty-seventh verse to the painful strains that can arise inside married life (`4:128–130`), the hundred and twenty-eighth verse was revealed when Sawdah bint Zam'ah—growing elderly and fearing that the Prophet might divorce her—offered to give her allotted day to 'A'ishah so that she could remain among his wives, and when other women feared estrangement or divorce from husbands who favored a younger wife. "If a woman fears indifference or neglect from her husband, there is no blame on either of them if they seek ˹fair˺ settlement" establishes that when a wife senses coldness, aversion, or impending separation from her husband, both spouses are completely free of sin if they reach a mutual compromise between themselves—without the meddling of outsiders—in which the wife voluntarily waives part of her financial maintenance or her turn of nights and the husband keeps her in the bond of marriage with honor and companionship. "which is best" proclaims a sweeping principle of Islamic law and family life: amicable settlement and reconciliation are better with Allah than stubborn contention, hostility, and divorce, so long as the agreement does not make the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful. "Humans are ever inclined to selfishness" diagnoses the root of marital and human conflict—souls are naturally prone to stinginess and clinging tightly to every personal claim, whether a wife refusing to yield any share or a husband begrudging companionship when his affection cools—and calls both spouses to overcome that greed through generosity. "But if you are gracious and mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Aware of what you do" urges husbands and wives alike to rise to an even higher station than mere legal compromise by bearing with one another in kindness, patience, and God-consciousness, promising that Allah knows every hidden sacrifice and will reward it beyond imagination, and reminding every married couple that when each partner looks past personal selfishness, protects the privacy of their home from third-party interference, and chooses either mutual concession or patient forbearance for the sake of God, Allah restores balance to their union and grants them a reward far greater than whatever right they waived, establishing a merciful precedent through the household of the Prophet himself by which couples across every age can preserve companionship, dignity, and mutual peace instead of rushing into bitter separation, before the hundred and twenty-ninth verse clarifies what kind of equality between wives lies within human power.

**Mutual settlement when a wife fears aversion and the precedent of Sawdah bint Zam'ah.**

(If a woman) i.e. 'Umayrah (feareth) is aware of (ill treatment) i.e. refrains from having sex with her (from her husband) As'ad Ibn al-Rabi', (or desertion) not speaking or sitting with her, (it is no sin for them twain) the man and the woman (if they make terms of peace between themselves) between the husband and wife whereby both of them are made content. (Peace) such that the wife is pleased (is better) than transgression and aversion. If a woman fears that her husband will ignore her and lose interest in her, there is no sin in them reaching a compromise where the woman gives up some of the rights due to her, such as maintenance and accommodation. In such a case, reconciliation is better than divorce. This was revealed regarding the case of a woman who does not bear children for her husband and, because of this, he wants to divorce her; or it could be about a women who has friends and children whom she does not like to be separated from and so she tells her husband who intends to divorce her: 'Do not divorce me; keep me with you and, in exchange, I forgo all the rights due to me'. Do not divorce me, and you are free to apportion for me whatever you like . And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse (If a woman feareth ill treatment from her husband). In the first case, when the wife fears that her husband is steering away from her or deserting her, she is allowed to forfeit all or part of her rights, such as provisions, clothing, dwelling, and so forth, and the husband is allowed to accept such concessions from her. Hence, there is no harm if she offers such concessions, and if her husband accepts them. Ibn 'Abbas said, "Whatever (legal agreement) the spouses mutually agree to is allowed.". In the Two Sahihs, it is recorded that 'A'ishah said that when Sawdah bint Zam'ah became old, she forfeited her day to 'A'ishah, and the Prophet used to spend Sawdah's night with 'A'ishah. (And if a woman fears cruelty or desertion on her husband's part), that it refers to, "A man who is married to an old woman, and he does not desire her and wants to divorce her. However, the apparent wording of the Ayah refers to the settlement where the wife forfeits some of the rights she has over her husband, with the husband agreeing to this concession, and that this settlement is better than divorce. For instance, the Prophet kept Sawdah bint Zam'ah as his wife after she offered to forfeit her day for 'A'ishah. By keeping her among his wives, his Ummah may follow this kind of settlement.

**Why reconciliation between the two spouses is better and how to overcome human selfishness.**

God exalted be He in explaining the natural disposition of man says But greed has been made present in the souls al-shuhh is extreme niggardliness meaning that they have a natural propensity for this as if they the souls are ever in its presence never absent from it. The meaning is a woman would scarcely allow another to share her husband with her and a man would scarcely allow her to enjoy him if he were to fall in love with another. (But greed hath been made present in the minds) souls are naturally inclined to be parsimonious, such that the wife withholds the share of her husband; it is also said that this means: her greed drives her to be pleased. Souls have been naturally created with greed and miserliness, and will not be keen to give up any right. The couple should, therefore, deal with this characteristic by training the soul to be forgiving and generous. Verses 128-130 which begin with the words: ‌ (And if a woman fears ill treatment or aversion from her husband ...) and end at (... All-Embracing, All-Wise) carry instructions about the painful and hard part of married life which is faced by every married couple during one or the other stage of their long association. For example, a husband does not have amorous feelings in his heart for his wife and she has no control over the means which could change his heart. It means that the husband and wife should enter into a compromise in between them. Here, the word (between the two of them) suggests that it is better if no third person interferes in husband-wife matters - let the two of them come to mutual compromise on some basis. This is because the injection of a third person may, at times, make the very compromise impossible. Thus, on the one hand, the Holy Qur'an gives to both parties the legal right to remove difficulties from their relationship and to receive their due right; while, on the other, by prompting both of them to demonstrate high morals and to be patient with the loss of their rights, the instruction given was that they should abstain from severing their relationship to the farthest limit of possibility. Initially, this verse simply mentions that compromise is permissible in the event of a husband-wife difference and towards the end of the verse, the parties have been prompted to carry on with the relationship in the best spirit of patience and forbearance in the event that such a compromise does not materialize. Thus, the parties would fare better if they avoid being stubborn about the fulfillment of their demands in toto and elect to forgo some of these from each side and agree to a compromise on some middle ground. "Every compromise is permissible between Muslims except a compromise in which something unlawful has been made lawful or something lawful has been made unlawful and Muslims must abide by accepted conditions except a condition in which something lawful has been made unlawful. If a woman makes a compromise by surrendering some of her rights, this compromise will totally eliminate the right of the woman the fulfill-ment of which stood incumbent on the husband at the time of the compromise. And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or rejection iʿrāḌ they are not at fault if they are reconciled through some agreement; reconciliation is better. But greed has been made present in the souls.

**Rising to graciousness, patience, and mindfulness of Allah in married life.**

If you are virtuous in your conjugal life with women and fear being unjust to them surely God is ever aware of what you do and He will requite you for it. (If ye do good) if you are equal in your treatment of the young wife and the elderly wife in the estates and maintenance (and keep from evil) avoid transgression and aversion, (Lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do) of transgression and aversion. If you do good in your affairs and are mindful of Allah, by fulfilling His instructions and avoiding His prohibitions, then Allah knows what you do. Nothing is hidden from Him and He will reward you accordingly. (But if you do good and have Taqwa, verily, Allah is Ever Well-Acquainted with what you do) if you are patient with the wife you dislike and treat her as other wives are treated, then Allah knows what you do and will reward you for it perfectly. The meaning of what has been said is: 'But, if you keep the fear of Allah in your heart and elect to be gracefully benign in your conduct and carry on accommodatingly with the relationship despite your emotional incompatibility and keep fulfilling her rights as due, then, this excellent conduct of yours is before Allah, the result of which is obvious. Almighty Allah will reward you for your forbearance and for the graces of your good deeds with blessings you can never imagine Perhaps, this is the reason why the text stops at; 'Allah is all-aware of what you do.' It does not spell out the return for the good deed. But whoever returns to God in his heart his affair will be restored to balance as a whole and in its particulars. If you are virtuous: [This] means that would be better for you. Surely God is ever aware of what you do: [This] means that once you have been annihilated from yourselves and your acts God suffices as Knower [4:70] after your annihilation and He suffices as the Giver of existence fol lowing your effacement. When people asked the Prophet about the injunctions of the shariah on various social matters, he was instructed by God that great emphasis must be laid on goodness, justice, fraternity and piety. This is because any law serves its purpose only when the person who has to enforce it is God-fearing and truly desirous of justice. Moreover, social reform can take place only when the evil-doer realizes that he is ultimately accountable to God and that, even if he manages to fool the people and save himself from the consequences of his crime in this world, he cannot escape from God’s grip. The dread of Hell will deter him from injustice and the hope of Paradise will give him the courage to endure the loss which is invariably faced in the process of living a truthful life.

129.text:
Clarifying the obligation of justice between wives first laid down in verse 3 of this surah—and continuing the guidance on marital strain from the hundred and twenty-eighth verse—the hundred and twenty-ninth verse distinguishes between the inner feelings of the heart, which no human being can force into exact equality, and the outward rights of companionship and maintenance, which lie squarely within a husband's control. "You will never be able to maintain ˹emotional˺ justice between your wives—no matter how keen you are" lifts the unbearable burden of equalizing inner love and attraction by acknowledging that even when a righteous husband divides his nights, housing, and spending with scrupulous fairness—as the Prophet himself did before praying, "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control"—the heart naturally inclines more deeply toward one spouse than another. "So do not totally incline towards one leaving the other in suspense" draws the strict legal boundary that every husband must obey: he must never let his inner preference spill over into outward injustice by turning away from his other wife in time, maintenance, and care so that she is left hanging like a prisoner—neither a cared-for wife with a husband nor a divorced woman free to marry someone else. "And if you do what is right and are mindful ˹of Allah˺, surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful" promises that when a husband sets right his outward dealings in fairness, fears harming his wives, and makes Allah his primary concern, Allah forgives the involuntary leanings of the heart and covers past shortcomings with mercy, before the hundred and thirtieth verse addresses the final case where marriage ends in separation.

**Why equalizing inner love is beyond human control while outward justice remains obligatory.**

You will never be able to be just to to treat equally your wives in terms of love even if you be eager for this; yet do not turn altogether away towards the one you love with respect to the shares and maintenance expenses so that you leave her the one from whom you turn away like one suspended one that is neither a slavegirl nor a woman with a husband. (Ye will not be able to deal equally between (your) wives) as regards love, (however much ye wish (to do so) even if you exert your efforts: You, husbands, will not be able to be completely fair to your wives with respect to your affection, even if you tried to do so. This is due to circumstances and factors beyond your control. Even when one divides the nights justly between wives, there will still be various degrees concerning love, desire and sexual intimacy, as Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ubaydah As-Salmani, Mujahid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim stated. Imam Ahmad and the collectors of the Sunan recorded that 'A'ishah said, "The Messenger of Allah used to treat his wives equally and proclaim,. (O Allah! This is my division in what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not own) referring to his heart. (And you shall never be able to maintain real equality between wives ... -129) which carries a special instruction for both. At this point it will be recalled that the Holy Qur'an has already established in the beginning of Surah al-Nis-a' that a man who holds more than one wife in the bond of marriage is duty-bond to maintain justice and equality among all wives, and that if one thinks that he would be unable to fulfill this obligation, he should not take more than one wife. O Allah, this equalization of mine is in what I have in my control, therefore, do not make me answerable for what is in Your control (that is, emotional inclination) and not in mine. The veneer of the words in verse 3 of Surah al-Nis-a' gave' the impression that maintaining equity between wives was ark absolute obligation which, obviously, includes equity in emotional inclination while this is something not in one's control. This is because the words mean: 'Even though maintaining equality in emotional inclination is not within your power, yet you should not lean totally towards one of your wives so much so that you start preferring her even in matters which lie within your power and control'. Instead, what is obligatory is the equality in matters which do lie in one's power and discretion.

**The prohibition of inclining completely to one wife and leaving the other suspended.**

(But turn not altogether away) with your bodies ((from one) in favour of the young wife, (leaving her) the other one: the old wife (as in suspense) like a prisoner: neither unmarried nor married. So do not incline fully away from the one you do not love and leave her like a woman suspended, who does not have a husband to fulfill her right and nor is she unmarried so that she may seek to marry another. (so do not incline too much to one of them) means, when you like one of your wives more than others, do not exaggerate in treating her that way,. (so as to leave the other hanging.) referring to the other wives. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas, As-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said that Mu'allaqah [hanging] means, "She is neither divorced nor married." (Whoever has two wives and inclines to one of them (too much), will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides dragging.) Allah's statement,. You will never be able to be just to your wives even if you are eager; yet do not turn altogether away so that you leave her like one suspended. Yet do not turn altogether away: [This] means do not deviate from the clear path of the command. So that you leave her like one suspended: [This] means that when you prevent them from being with someone other than you even as you cut them off from any share of you you harm [them] in two ways for there is nothing to be had from you and there [is] no way for them to be with someone else.

**Setting affairs right in mindfulness of Allah and receiving His forgiveness and mercy.**

If you set things right by being just with the shares and fear injustice surely God is ever Forgiving regarding the inclination in your hearts Merciful to you in this respect. (If ye do good and keep from evil) if you treat them equally and avoid transgression and aversion, (lo! Allah is ever Forgiving) of those who repent of transgression and aversion, (Merciful) towards those who die in a state of repentance. If you set things right between yourselves, by giving the wife her due right and being mindful of Allah in that regard, then Allah will be Forgiving and Merciful towards you. (And if you do justice, and do all that is right and have Taqwa, then Allah is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.) The Ayah states: If you do justice and divide equally in what you have power over, while fearing Allah in all conditions, then Allah will forgive you the favoritism that you showed to some of your wives. If you set things right and fear surely God is ever Forgiving Merciful. [This] means when your concern is for yourself in your affairs the state of your union together is overturned and what was sound becomes ruined. But when you have made God your concern in your affairs the balance of your life together will be restored and at that time will be cleared of turmoil. If you set things right between you and other created beings wa-in tuṣliḥū mā baynakum wa-bayna al-khalq and put your trust in what is between you and the Real wa-tathiqū fīmā baynakum wa-bayna al-ḥaqq surely God is ever forgiving of your failings fa-inna Allāha ghafūrun li-ʿuyūbikum merciful in pardoning your sins raḥīmun bi-l-ʿafwi ʿan dhunūbikum. The differences emerging between husband and wife or between any other two persons largely result from greed. The proper course is for each party to give thought to the other’s problems and making due allowances, try to reach some consensus. God does not seize man for his natural weaknesses but rather takes man to task for his deliberate excesses and acts of injustice out of haughtiness and insolence. If man fears God and has the urge of reform in his heart, all his acts done with the right intentions would be considered pardonable in the Hereafter.

130.text:
Completing the three-verse guidance on marital discord (`4:128–130`) after the hundred and twenty-eighth and hundred and twenty-ninth verses encouraged mutual settlement, patience, and outward fairness, the hundred and thirtieth verse addresses the third situation—when every honest effort at harmony fails and parting becomes the wisest course—and removes the fear of destitution or ruin that often turns divorce into bitter warfare. "But if they choose to separate, Allah will enrich both of them from His bounties" reassures both the husband and the wife that if they part ways through divorce or mutual release, neither spouse's livelihood or future happiness depends on the other; out of His vast provision, Allah will make each of them independent of the other, blessing the woman with a new home, provision, or a more suitable husband and blessing the man with peace of mind and a more compatible wife. "And Allah is Ever-Bountiful, All-Wise" seals the passage by affirming that Allah's grace and capacity are boundless and that His legislation—including permitting separation when a marriage can no longer fulfill its purpose—flows from perfect wisdom, reminding both spouses that just as Allah united them when they were once strangers to one another, His all-encompassing generosity can open new doors of peace, sustenance, and righteous companionship for each of them after they part in fairness, before the hundred and thirty-first verse anchors all moral and legal duties in Allah's ownership of the heavens and the earth.

**How Allah enriches both spouses out of His vast bounty when marriage ends in separation.**

But if they the married couple separate by way of divorce God will compensate each of them from the need of the other out of His plenty that is out of His bounty by giving her another as husband and giving him another as wife. God is ever Embracing of His creatures in bounty Wise in what He has ordained for them. (But if they separate) i.e. the man and the woman through divorce, (Allah will compensate each) the man and the woman (out of His abundance) from His provision: the man will be compensated with another wife and the woman with another husband. (Allah is ever All-Embracing) in relation to them as regards marriage, (All-Knowing) of that which He prescribed for them of justice. If a couple separate by divorce (issued by the man) or khul‘ (initiated by the woman), then Allah will make each one of them rich through His vast Bounty: He will enrich the man with a wife that is more suitable for him; and He will enrich the woman with a husband that is more suitable for her. (But if they separate (divorce), Allah will provide abundance for everyone of them from His bounty. And Allah is Ever All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Wise.) This is the third case between husband and wife, in which divorce occurs. Allah states that if the spouses separate by divorce, then Allah will suffice them by giving him a better wife and her a better husband. (And Allah is Ever All-Sufficient for His creatures' needs, All-Wise.) is: His favor is tremendous, His bounty is enormous and He is All-Wise in all His actions, decisions and commandments.

**Maintaining justice in marriage and trusting Allah's provision when separation is needed.**

In order to make married life pleasant and stable, the Holy Qur'an has given important instructions to both parties in these verses. At this point it will be recalled that the Holy Qur'an has already established in the beginning of Surah al-Nis-a' that a man who holds more than one wife in the bond of marriage is duty-bond to maintain justice and equality among all wives, and that if one thinks that he would be unable to fulfill this obligation, he should not take more than one wife. O Allah, this equalization of mine is in what I have in my control, therefore, do not make me answerable for what is in Your control (that is, emotional inclination) and not in mine. The veneer of the words in verse 3 of Surah al-Nis-a' gave' the impression that maintaining equity between wives was ark absolute obligation which, obviously, includes equity in emotional inclination while this is something not in one's control. Therefore, in this verse of the Surah al-Nisa', the matter was clarified by saying that in things which one does not control, equality is not obligatory. However, equality shall be observed in matters within one's control, for example, equality in spending nights with them, their living standards and cost of maintenance. This is because the words mean: 'Even though maintaining equality in emotional inclination is not within your power, yet you should not lean totally towards one of your wives so much so that you start preferring her even in matters which lie within your power and control'. As'ad Ibn al-Rabi' had another young wife whom he favoured, and Allah forbade him from doing so and commanded that the young and the old wives were treated equally. And if you do justice, and do all that is right and have Taqwa, then Allah is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful But if they separate (by divorce), Allah will provide abundance for everyone of them from His bounty. In the first case, when the wife fears that her husband is steering away from her or deserting her, she is allowed to forfeit all or part of her rights, such as provisions, clothing, dwelling, and so forth, and the husband is allowed to accept such concessions from her. (But if you do good and have Taqwa, verily, Allah is Ever Well-Acquainted with what you do) if you are patient with the wife you dislike and treat her as other wives are treated, then Allah knows what you do and will reward you for it perfectly.

**Realizing that every servant's true need is for God alone and avoiding arrogance.**

The essential companionship is the companionship of the heart in per petual need of God since there is no separating oneself from the Real. As for everything other than the Real [human beings] have no need for one another except in the external sense-this is the thinking of those in a state of separation aṣḥāb al-tafriqa. As for the people of realization ahl al-taḥqīq they have no doubt that the need of created beings is entirely for God . The differences emerging between husband and wife or between any other two persons largely result from greed. The proper course is for each party to give thought to the other’s problems and making due allowances, try to reach some consensus. Just as God desires people to be considerate to one another, similarly He shows the maximum consideration to His servants. God does not seize man for his natural weaknesses but rather takes man to task for his deliberate excesses and acts of injustice out of haughtiness and insolence. Besides, one should never nurture such thoughts in his mind that it is he who is behind the success of such and such a person and that if he had not helped that person, success could never have been achieved.
